analysis.title: GS Basics: Bonds Up/AI Down. Neoclouds. Computer Inflation. 15 Oct 2026
key_insights: KOSPI fell 8% and triggered circuit breakers, with the AI trade the focus. The author says the prior pain trade was long AI / short bonds, and both sides are now unwinding.
Credit concerns have entered the AI spending picture, and the market is increasingly reading this as a growth shock. Crowding out is showing up through the marginal borrower.
GS's global neocloud basket is down 20% in five sessions, roughly a 1st percentile move over ten years, with selling accelerating. Hyperscaler IG spreads widened another 7.4bp last week.
If appetite to finance the AI buildout is constrained, the result is slower chip consumption, less capex and weaker growth.
TSMC reported revenue of $46.7bn, EPS NT$29.43 and gross margin of 66.4%. Margins were slightly light but within guidance. The debate has moved from demand to supply.

CPI: shelter was firmer, but the author doubts housing inflation is accelerating given the housing market and homebuilders. The bigger concern is a pickup in broader services inflation, which may reflect second-order energy effects and makes the Fed's job harder.
October Fed odds settled around 30%. PPI and Warsh are the events to watch, and the author's gut view is that the Fed waits until December.
The author does not see a demand crisis in AI. Aggregate token consumption keeps surprising to the upside, and scarce compute favours well-capitalized hyperscalers.
An open question is whether hyperscalers fund added capacity from balance-sheet equity and operating cash flow rather than debt markets, which would ease debt overhang concerns.

Physical delivery (power, energized data centers, gigawatts) is the harder part to falsify, with constraints becoming more tangible in 2027 and 2028. Logistics, permitting and policy are messy, creating execution risk for middlemen and explaining the derating across the complex.
Demand for compute can grow exponentially but the capital to finance it cannot. This favours powered capacity and strong balance sheets over leveraged middlemen.

A lot of bad news is priced: neoclouds fell 20% in five sessions, while quality has rallied in 16 of 18 sessions with RSI at 83. Discretionary nets are low and rates are rallying. The author thinks pockets have been overdone and that stable-to-lower rates would help.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand for compute keeps growing, aggregate token consumption is surprising to the upside, positioning and valuations are more supportive, and lower rates would improve the financing equation.
tension_points.bear_case: Capital available to finance the buildout is limited, neocloud selling is accelerating and hyperscaler IG spreads are widening, which could slow chip consumption and capex and weaken growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If rates fail to stabilize lower or credit spreads keep widening across the AI vertical, the financing-constraint case strengthens.
